title: Strength training for the treatment of Cushing's associated myopathy: a randomised study
summary: Endogenous Cushing's Syndrome is a rare disease with severe comorbidities, such as Cushing's associated myopathy. This is often persistent in patients with Cushing's Syndrome despite successful therapy, which has an Impact on the Quality of life in the affected patients. The aim of this randomized, interventional study is to better understand Cushing's associated myopathy and the effects of physical Training on muscle function in this context.

interventions.name: Early intervention with individual physical training from 4 weeks after baseline/surgery to 13 months after baseline/surgery
Standard follow-up in the first 7 months after baseline/surgery and late intervention with 6 months of individual physical training until 13 months after baseline/surgery

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Cushing's syndrome:
- path. Dexamethasone inhibition test
- path. 23 o'clock salivary cortisol level
- path. 24h-collection urine cortisol 
- planned surgery
- Confirmed subtype: adrenal, pituitary or ectopic

Cushing's syndrome in long-term remission: 
- Successfully treated Cushing's syndrome
- Persisting functional impairment
Exclusion criteria:
- Age under 18 years or over 65 years
- Contraindication to surgery
- Existing pregnancy
- Chronic general illness
- Alcohol or drug abuse
- Physical limitation to participate in the exercise program 
- Participation in another interventional clinical trial
- Life expectancy of less than one year
- Myocardial infarction within the past 3 months
- Cardiopulmonary instability or ischemia signs during exercise testing
- Cytostatic therapy
